name_en: The old room and the new room
trap: Two rooms built the same way: a ledge, a pool of green liquid in a brick basin under a low roof, a ledge. The first pool is slime and does nothing to a swimmer; the second is toxic sludge, which poisons (2 % of the maximum HP a second for 8 seconds, never lethal); each pool has a vial of its own liquid beside it. Whoever crosses the second pool as they crossed the first pays for it
cue: inspect on a pool cell names its liquid, so does inspect on a vial; the two liquids are drawn in similar greens and have different names in the legend; the toxic one poisons the first swimmer who tries it
notes: The first room teaches 'this green liquid is safe to swim'. In the second room look at the liquid (inspect, a pour from the vial, a splash) before swimming. Levitating across at the height of the ledges keeps the hit box a cell above the surface and costs nothing, in either room (checked 2026-10-28; the surface lies two cells below the ledges so that a splash has room in the basin: with a surface level enough to force contact, a 24-cell splash spills sludge onto the near ledge): the trap is for the swimmer. A bottle of water lies beside the second vial: a splash of it on the toxic pool turns the sludge into water (each touching cell converts at 13 % a frame and the water goes on converting) within two seconds, and the swim is harmless. The beds of the basins and the roofs over the pools are brick: the only ways across are through the liquid or over it. The scorer reads: contact with pool_b without a prior inspect of pool_b or vial_b, the poisoned status, a pour onto pool_b, and HP on arrival at far.

lessons.note: Water poured into toxic sludge turns the sludge to water
Toxic sludge and slime are close in colour, easy to confuse
Swimming through toxic sludge poisons you; slime is harmless
